messages:
Priya: Customer (acct EGT-432) reported a sudden p99 increase ~06:12 UTC. They say most requests are routing to us-west-2 even though the workspace is EU. Trace ID: trace-abc123. Asking for help to triage.
Anna: Pasting customer's snippet and sample curl they used:
```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ \ 
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \ 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rm-large"}'
```
They attached a short trace excerpt: spans show egress ip 52.203.x.x and DNS resolved to api-us.redwood.example.com for ~30% of requests.
Rob: Looking. Pulled up traces via tracing-bot. I'm seeing a spike of cross-region hops starting at 06:11:55 UTC. Full trace: trace-abc123 -> host-eu-proxy -> egress-gw-us -> model-host-us.
tracing-bot: Waterfall for trace-abc123: 
- client -> edge-eu (latency 30ms)
- edge-eu -> route-service (health-check 500s)
- route-service -> egress-us (1200ms)
Reactions: :warning: on route-service line.
Mike: Quick question: any recent infra changes in EU POP? BGP updates? I see a noise event in our eu POP at 06:10 UTC — AS path flap with our CDN partner for ~90s. Could be upstream anycast reshuffle.
Priya: Customer says their requests were steady until 06:12 then p50->p99 went up and errors increased. They saw auth token rejections intermittently (probably due to latency/timeouts).
Rob: Two hypotheses: (1) upstream anycast/POP issue caused some DNS lookups to land on US anycast IPs, (2) internal smart-routing fallback triggered because the customer's dedicated pool instances in EU reported unhealthy or saturated. I'm checking dedicated pool metrics for EGT-432.
infra-bot: Dedicated pool EGT-432 (eu-west-1) usage: commit 50rps, actual 120rps at 06:11-06:13 -> overflow configured to allow fallback to hosted endpoint. Health: 3/5 instances reported degraded health (OOM-kill churn).
Anna: Customer confirms they ran a short stress test earlier for a spike and might have exceeded their reserved throughput. They didn't expect fallback.
Mike: That explains the region handoff path. If route-service sees degraded dedicated instances, routing policy allows fallback to any healthy regional pool (including US). Combined with CDN anycast, some DNS lookups prefer us endpoints. So two-layer failure: capacity + POP anycast drift -> cross-region latency.
Rob: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) Hit their workspace endpoint with X-Client-Region: eu-west-1 header and 200 concurrent requests.
2) Observed route-service mark instances unhealthy after 3s of queueing.
3) Requests routed to hosted pools (us) -> p99 spikes to ~1.2s.
Logs: 
```
[06:11:57] route-service: pool-check: eu-pool EGT-432 queue=130 status=degraded
[06:11:58] router: fallback -> hosted-us-modelpool
[06:11:58] egress-gw-us: connection established
```
Priya: Immediate mitigation options? Customer needs latency stabilized now.
Mike: Short-term: disable automated fallback for their route (will cause 429s if capacity exceeds) or expand their dedicated pool immediately. Recommend disabling fallback only if they can tolerate rejects. We can also pin DNS to eu edge for their account for a few minutes to avoid anycast drift, but that's brittle.
Anna: Customer prefers capacity increase over disables. Can we hot-add nodes?
infra-bot: Autoscale policy for their dedicated pool is manual; adding 4 nodes will take ~7 minutes to provision in eu-west-1. Can do now if OK.
Rob: While nodes spin up, we should reduce queueing by lowering max-concurrent-per-instance to reduce OOM churn (config change applies immediately). I'll patch canary to 2 instances in eu region (non-destructive) to relieve memory pressure.
Priya: Please proceed with both: provision + config patch. Keep me posted, I'm on call with customer.
Rob: Patch rolled out to 10% -> 50% -> 100% by 06:20. deploy-bot: rollout successful: router-config/update-concurrency v2 -> 100%.
infra-bot: Provision request submitted for +4 nodes in eu-west-1 for pool EGT-432. Expected ready 06:27 UTC.
Mike: Also bumped fallback weight for hosted-us to 0 for EGT-432 to prevent future US handoffs while scaling completes. Config applied.
tracing-bot: New traces show routing stayed in-eu after 06:22 for 100% of sampled requests. p99 back to ~140ms.
Anna: Customer confirms latency back to normal and auth errors cleared. They saw temporary 429s for ~30s during the earliest patch window but are ok.
Priya: Root cause summary for ticket: dedicated pool saturation (customer-induced spike) caused degraded instances + automated fallback to hosted pools. This combined with a transient anycast/BGP drift in EU POP resulted in a portion of requests resolving to US egress, producing cross-region p99 spikes and auth timeouts.
Priya: Action items:
- (Ops) Add alert when dedicated pool queue > 80% for >1m (Rob/infra).
- (Platform) Make fallback weight for cross-region default 0 for customer-dedicated pools, require explicit opt-in (Mike).
- (Docs) Update KB about reserved capacity overflow behavior and recommended autoscale/playbook (Anna).
- (CS) Follow up with customer about better spike protection and offer to schedule load test (Priya).
Mike: Noting also to follow up with CDN partner on the eu POP BGP noise; log ticket created: CDN-INC-5591.
Priya: Thanks team. Closing loop with customer now. :white_check_mark:
